title: Antioch Session v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1 was answered No (2-1): Presbytery did not err in approving Arthur Peterson for licensure. Issue 2 was answered Yes (3-0): Presbytery erred by allowing him to serve regularly as stated supply for at least six months without licensure. The licensure remained undisturbed, and Presbytery was enjoined to be more circumspect in the future.
first_summary: Antioch Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s approval of Arthur Peterson for licensure and its earlier allowance of his regular stated-supply preaching without licensure. The SJC upheld the licensure because Presbytery had thoroughly examined his divorce and theological views and had violated no established constitutional standard. It sustained the stated-supply issue because BCO 19-1 required licensure and enjoined Presbytery to exercise greater future circumspection.
summary: Antioch Session challenged Peterson’s licensure based on his prior divorce, creation and local-flood views, reversal of a committee recommendation, and close vote; it also challenged his regular preaching before licensure. The SJC rejected the licensure specifications because Presbytery had thoroughly examined repentance and doctrinal adherence, and no definitive PCA standard required exclusion on these facts. It sustained the pre-licensure supply issue under BCO 19-1, 22-5, and 22-6 and enjoined greater future circumspection. The licensure remained undisturbed; the ruling was expressly case-specific.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The General Assembly approved and adopted the SJC judgment in Case 92-9a; printed p. 88, lines 14–18.
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged both Peterson’s licensure and his prior regular service as stated supply without licensure; printed pp. 88–90, lines 20–40, 51–60.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issue 1 was No and Issue 2 Yes. The court found a thorough constitutional examination but a BCO violation concerning unlicensed pulpit supply; printed pp. 90–93, lines 44–47, 63–128.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority made its licensure ruling fact-specific and not binding for ordination or every doctrinal formulation; Issue 1 drew a dissent, while Issue 2 was unanimous; printed pp. 91–95, lines 81–87, 113–136, 188–202.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Earlier Assembly rulings and Cases 90-3, 90-8, and 91-5 were cited or distinguished; printed pp. 90–94, lines 65–71, 101–103, 168–178.
